stem: Which handoff best preserves an unresolved crop observation for the receiving shift?
choices: Zone B rechecked at 14:00; 4 of 12 sampled plants remain wilted; lead notified; improvement noted, so the issue is considered resolved unless symptoms return
Zone B rechecked at 14:00; 4 of 12 sampled plants remain wilted; cause unresolved; lead notified; next check due per work order
Zone B rechecked at 14:00; 4 of 12 sampled plants remain wilted; details explained verbally to the receiving technician, so no additional written follow-up is needed
Zone B rechecked at 14:00; 4 of 12 sampled plants remain wilted; observation recorded, but the next check is left open for the receiving shift to decide
rationale: A strong handoff preserves what was checked, the remaining observation, sample context, uncertainty, escalation and the next expected check. Partial improvement, verbal-only transfer or an unspecified next action can create continuity gaps.
